title: Kanem-Bornu
summary: Kanem, east of Lake Chad, arose as a confederation of nomadic peoples; Encyclopedia.com dates its rise to the eighth century, and al-Yaqubi first mentions it in 872. From about 1075 the Saifawa dynasty ruled, the court adopted Islam after long contact with Muslim traders, and Njimi became the capital. Trade in salt, copper, cotton, ivory and slaves crossed it, and Mai Dunama Dibbalemi expanded it with cavalry. Driven out by the Bulala around 1390, its kings founded Bornu west of the lake, which lasted until the late nineteenth century.

uncertainty.note: Encyclopedia.com: came to power in the eighth century; WHE: first textual mention in 872, the Bornu Empire lasted until the late 19th century, when the French took it over.

as_recorded.value: came to power during the eighth century c.e.
flourished from the 9th to 14th century CE

where.modern_name: Mao area, Kanem Region, Chad (historical Kanem heartland east of Lake Chad; the empire expanded across modern Chad, Nigeria, Niger, Cameroon, and Libya)
where.historical_name: Kanem, northeast of Lake Chad (ruled from Njimi; later centered in Bornu at Ngazargamu)

importance.justification: A Muslim trading empire of the Lake Chad basin for about a thousand years (R3 D3 T3 L2).
